answer: To secure an economy of autonomous agents against Sybil attacks, networks can implement a computational proof-of-stake anchored to a verifiable audit ledge. As the system demands locked economic capital for transaction validation, spinning up fake identities becomes economically prohibitive. Like marine organisms anchoring themselves to a coral reef to withstand a turbulent tide, genuine agents must tie real economic value to their cryptographic keys, ensuring that any unbacked, mass-generated entity is immediately washed out by the protocol's consensus rules.
